newsitem.title: USA: Micron says spot DRAM chip prices firmer.
newsitem.headline: Micron says spot DRAM chip prices firmer.

text.p: Micron Technology Inc President and Chief Executive Steven Appleton on Tuesday said spot prices for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips have risen about 50 percent since Korean suppliers revealed plans to limit output.
"The pricing the last few weeks is up about 50 percent,"
he told investors at a Robertson Stephens technology conference in San Francisco. He said spot prices for DRAM chips were currently about $9 to $9.50.
Appleton also said the company had only a limited amount of unsold inventory on its books.
He said he believed Korean companies would act on their recent statements about curbing production of DRAM chips.
"I think the intent on the Korean market is real," he said. "We've been saying for some time that there isn't such an imbalance between supply and demand."

"We don't have unsold inventory of any significance," he added, saying he expected further growth in the DRAM market as customers switch to more memory-intensive Microsoft Windows NT and Intel Pentium MMX multimedia processors.
"We are one of the few that's still making money in the DRAM area," said Appleton.
He declined to comment on financial estimates, noting the company's second fiscal quarter would close at the end of the week.
Analyst forecasts range from a loss of $0.05 a share to a profit of $0.21. Some observers expected Micron to get a boost toward the end of the quarter thanks to firmer pricing.

Micron executives declined comment on future pricing in the volatile chip memory market. Appleton earlier gave a keynote address in which he said people within the industry have long predicted an end to the cyclical nature of the business, though that had yet to occur.

"I hear these myths all the time," he said. "I always hear there's never going to be another downturn, and I hear there's never going to be another upturn -- from my own guys as well as our competitors."
